facts.statement: The genus Tubonasus was described by Dennis and Miles in 1979.
Tubonasus lived during the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
Fossils of Tubonasus date from 382.31 to 379 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tubonasus is an extinct genus of long-snouted arthrodire placoderm known only from one species.
facts.quote: Tubonasus (meaning "tube nose") is an extinct monospecific genus of long-snouted arthrodire placoderm

facts.statement: Tubonasus fossils have been found in the Gogo Formation of Kimberley, Western Australia.
facts.quote: found at the Gogo Formation of Kimberley, Western Australia.

facts.statement: Researchers interpret Tubonasus as a pelagic pursuit predator capable of swallowing prey whole.
facts.quote: Tubonasus is interpreted as a pelagic pursuit predator, and had the ability of swallowing prey whole.

facts.statement: Tubonasus possessed an elongated rostrum, a streamlined body, and narrow infragnathals.
facts.quote: Like other camuropiscids, it has an elongated rostrum, streamlined body, and narrow infragnathals.

facts.statement: Tubonasus belongs to the family Camuropiscidae, the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, and the clade Coccosteomorphi.
facts.quote: Tubonasus is a member of the family Camuropiscidae under the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: Tubonasus is classified within the class Placodermi.
